## Create denitrification equation

This script is for creating a denitrification equation from paired nitrate, soil organic carbon and denitrification data so we can predict denitrification rates using nitrate and soil organic carbon data, which are more easily measured.

## 1. Set up

Get packages.

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(readxl)
library(plotly)
```

Get data.

```{r data}
denit <- read_excel(here("Data/Denitrification_NO3_SOC.xlsx"), sheet = "for_R")
```

## 2. Run multiple regression

Visualise relationships between predictors.

```{r explore}
ggplot(denit, aes(x = NOx_mgL, y = Dw_mg_m2_hr)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

ggplot(denit, aes(x = NOx_mgL, y = Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # Dtot looks like a better fit

ggplot(denit, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Dw_mg_m2_hr)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

ggplot(denit, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 
```

Manipulate. Make log versions of variables.

```{r manipulate}
denit <- denit %>% mutate(
  Log_Dtot = log10(Dtot),
  Log_NOx = log10(NOx_mgL),
  Log_Dw = log10(Dw_mg_m2_hr)
)

# visualise with these new variables
ggplot(denit, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dtot, color = Site)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # better fit

ggplot(denit, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dtot, color = Site)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# Dw
ggplot(denit, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dw, color = Site)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") # better fit

ggplot(denit, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dw, color = Site)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 
```

Make a model with all the data. These include data from other locations in Queensland from previous studies.

```{r model}
m <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit)
plot(m) # assumptions look fine

summary(m)

# equation is Log(Dtot) = 1.4360 + 0.4241 * Log(NOx) + 0.0098 * Soil_OC
# R squared adjusted = 0.58
```

I think too large geographic locations... Try with only Maroochy estuary data.

```{r model_maroochy_only}
denit_maroochy <- denit %>% dplyr::filter(Site %in% c("Yandina", "Blue Heart"))

# visualise
ggplot(denit_maroochy, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

ggplot(denit_maroochy, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# visualise Dw
ggplot(denit_maroochy, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dw)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

ggplot(denit_maroochy, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dw)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# model
m2 <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit_maroochy)
plot(m2) # assumptions look fine

summary(m2)

# equation is log(Dtot) = 1.6030 + 0.6975 * Log(NO3) + 0.0062 * Soil_OC
# R squared adjusted = 0.9117

# what happens when we remove SOC% as a variable?
m2.1 <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ Log_NOx, data = denit_maroochy)
anova(m2, m2.1) # model with SOC has lower RSS, therefore retain as it better explains variance.




# try with Dw
# model
m2.5 <- lm(Log_Dw ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit_maroochy)
plot(m2.5) # assumptions look fine

summary(m2.5) # way worse fit - confirms that Dtot is better.

# equation is 0.9286 + 0.7048 * Log(NO3) + 0.0008 * Soil_OC
# R squared adjusted = 0.5124
```

Also try with just the latest Blue Heart data.

```{r model_blueheart}
denit_blueheart <- denit %>% dplyr::filter(Site == "Blue Heart")

# visualise
ggplot(denit_blueheart, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

ggplot(denit_blueheart, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dtot)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# visualise
ggplot(denit_blueheart, aes(x = Log_NOx, y = Log_Dw)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

ggplot(denit_blueheart, aes(x = `OC_%_`, y = Log_Dw)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

# model
m4 <- lm(Log_Dtot ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit_blueheart)
plot(m4) # assumptions look fine

summary(m4) # not enough power anymore! variables not significant

# equation is 
# R squared adjusted = 0.77

# model Dw
m4.5 <- lm(Log_Dw ~ `OC_%_` + Log_NOx, data = denit_blueheart)
plot(m4.5) # assumptions look fine

summary(m4.5)  # not enough power anymore! variables not significant
```

Therefore, use m2 (best fit)!

## 3. Plot

Plot the model results - planar relationship between the three variables.

```{r 3D plot}
# Create a grid of values for the plane
NOx_seq <- seq(min(denit_maroochy$Log_NOx), max(denit_maroochy$Log_NOx), length.out = 20)
SOC_seq <- seq(min(denit_maroochy$`OC_%_`), max(denit_maroochy$`OC_%_`), length.out = 20)
grid <- expand.grid(Log_NOx = NOx_seq, `OC_%_` = SOC_seq)

# Add predictions to the grid and convert to matrix format
grid$Log_Dtot <- predict(m2, newdata = grid)
z_matrix <- matrix(grid$Log_Dtot, nrow = 20, ncol = 20)

# Plot the points and the regression plane
plane_plot <- plot_ly(data = denit_maroochy, x = ~Log_NOx, y = ~`OC_%_`, z = ~Log_Dtot, 
                      type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers") %>%
              add_surface(x = ~NOx_seq, y = ~SOC_seq, z = ~z_matrix, 
                          opacity = 0.5) %>% 
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Log NOx"),
         yaxis = list(title = "SOC (%)"
    #zaxis = list(title = "Denitrification (mg/m2/hr)"),
    ))
plane_plot 


```

Also plot Dw in 3D.

```{r 3D_plot_Dw}
# Create a grid of values for the plane
NOx_seq <- seq(min(denit_maroochy$Log_NOx), max(denit_maroochy$Log_NOx), length.out = 20)
SOC_seq <- seq(min(denit_maroochy$`OC_%_`), max(denit_maroochy$`OC_%_`), length.out = 20)
grid <- expand.grid(Log_NOx = NOx_seq, `OC_%_` = SOC_seq)

# Add predictions to the grid and convert to matrix format
grid$Log_Dw <- predict(m2.5, newdata = grid)
z_matrix <- matrix(grid$Log_Dw, nrow = 20, ncol = 20)

# Plot the points and the regression plane
plane_plot_dw <- plot_ly(data = denit_maroochy, x = ~Log_NOx, y = ~`OC_%_`, z = ~Log_Dw, 
                      type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers") %>%
              add_surface(x = ~NOx_seq, y = ~SOC_seq, z = ~z_matrix, 
                          opacity = 0.5) %>% 
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Log NOx"),
         yaxis = list(title = "SOC (%)"
    #zaxis = list(title = "Denitrification (mg/m2/hr)"),
    ))
plane_plot_dw 
```
